findings.problem: loadHTTPRoute and loadGRPCRoute (grpcroute.go:24) are line-for-line copies. Both walk the parentRef/listener loop, build the Accepted/ResolvedRefs conditions, call attachedRoutes.Conflicts/Record, check servedRules.register and record the parent status. The only differences are the route kind, the config loader and the status recorder. Any fix to the attachment logic must be made twice.
findings.fix: Extract one helper, e.g. attachHTTPRoute(ctx, kind, meta, parentRefs, hostnames, loadConf func(listener, hostnames) ([]routeRouter, metav1.Condition), record func(gatev1.RouteParentStatus)). Call it from both loadHTTPRoute and loadGRPCRoute.

findings.problem: grpcRouteRouter, httpRouteRouter (httproute.go:126), tlsRouteRouter (tlsroute.go:134) and tcpRouteRouter (tcproute.go:118) are four identical {Name string; Conf *dynamic.Configuration} types.
findings.fix: Replace the four types with a single routeRouter type in kubernetes.go and use it in all four route files.

findings.problem: The BackendTLSPolicy handling is copied three times: in loadHTTPServers, loadGRPCServers (grpcroute.go:374) and loadTLSServers (tlsroute.go:361). Each copy sorts the policies, filters targetRefs by name and sectionName, builds the PolicyAncestorStatus, writes the conflict/accepted conditions and returns the route error condition. The new client-certificate injection was also added to each copy separately.
findings.fix: Extract a generic helper, e.g. resolveBackendTLSPolicy[T any](gatewayName, gatewayNamespace, namespace string, listener gatewayListener, backendName gatev1.ObjectName, svcPort corev1.ServicePort, route metav1.Object, load func(*gatev1.BackendTLSPolicy) (T, metav1.Condition), statusReport) (T, *metav1.Condition). It owns the sorting, ancestor statuses and error condition. The three loaders then only build the load balancer and apply listener.BackendClientCertificate.

findings.problem: loadTCPServersTransport duplicates loadServersTransport (httproute.go:789): the SAN mapping, the WellKnownCACertificates shortcut and the ConfigMap/Secret ca.crt resolution, with the same conditions. Only the target struct differs.
findings.fix: Extract resolveBackendTLSValidation(namespace, policy) (serverName string, sans []tls.SAN, insecureSkipVerify bool, rootCAs []types.FileOrContent, metav1.Condition). Make both functions thin wrappers that fill dynamic.ServersTransport or dynamic.TLSClientConfig from its result.

findings.problem: The Gateway and ListenerSet sorts (lines 456 and 465) inline the same creation-time/namespace/name comparator that compareRoutes (line 1758) already implements for any metav1.Object.
findings.fix: Rename compareRoutes to compareByCreation(a, b metav1.Object) int. Use it in both sorts, e.g. slices.SortStableFunc(gateways, func(a, b *gatev1.Gateway) int { return compareByCreation(a, b) }).

findings.problem: gatewayForOwner and matchingGatewayListenersForParentRef (line 1885) repeat the same inline check that a listener belongs to a given ListenerSet owner (nil check plus namespace/name comparison).
findings.fix: Add a method func (o listenerOwner) declares(l gatewayListener) bool that covers both the Gateway case and the ListenerSet case. Use it in both functions.

findings.problem: loadGatewayListeners resolves the Gateway's frontend validations (default and per-port) on every call. Because it is now also called once per ListenerSet, the same ConfigMap and ReferenceGrant lookups run again for every ListenerSet of the Gateway. A function meant to load listeners also owns Gateway-level TLS resolution.
findings.fix: Resolve the default and per-port frontendValidation once per Gateway in loadConfigurationFromGateways, the same way resolveBackendClientCertificate is handled. Pass the result into loadGatewayListeners, for example as a field of listenerClaims or a dedicated parameter.

findings.problem: The expression that decides whether the listener is in Passthrough mode is repeated at tlsroute.go:164 and tlsroute.go:474. tcproute.go:149 uses a variant without the nil check on listener.TLS.
findings.fix: Add func (l gatewayListener) isTLSPassthrough() bool { return l.TLS != nil && ptr.Deref(l.TLS.Mode, gatev1.TLSModeTerminate) == gatev1.TLSModePassthrough } and use it at all three sites.

findings.problem: withoutForeignConditions and mergeGatewayStatus (line 860) each hand-code the 'type not in gatewayConditionTypes/listenerConditionTypes' predicate. listenersStatusEqual (line 953) and listenerEntryStatusesEqual (line 976) are identical apart from the element type.
findings.fix: Add helpers isOwnedGatewayCondition(c) and isOwnedListenerCondition(c) and use them in both functions. Implement listenerEntryStatusesEqual by converting each entry with gatev1.ListenerStatus(entry), as makeListenerSetStatus already does in reverse, then delegating to listenersStatusEqual.

findings.problem: UpdateGRPCRouteStatus formats its error as %q with route.Name only. The other Update*Status methods use namespace/name.
findings.fix: Change the call to fmt.Errorf("failed to update GRPCRoute %s/%s status: %w", route.Namespace, route.Name, err).

findings.problem: loadHTTPRouteConfiguration inlines about 30 lines that parse timeouts.request and timeouts.backendRequest into RouterRespondingTimeouts and ForwardingTimeouts. This makes the per-rule loop hard to follow. Retry parsing is already extracted (loadHTTPRouteRetry).
findings.fix: Extract loadHTTPRouteTimeouts(ctx, *gatev1.HTTPRouteTimeouts) (*dynamic.RouterRespondingTimeouts, *dynamic.ForwardingTimeouts) next to loadHTTPRouteRetry and call it once per rule.

A function meant to load listeners also owns Gateway-level TLS resolution.
